meta.title: Step 5F Pilot — Primary Number Manipulatives (construction-lab 1.7.0)
meta.subject: Mathematics (NaCCA Primary B1–B6 & Cambridge Primary)
meta.topic: Primary Number Manipulatives v1.7.0 Verification (18 slides: CPA Ten Frames, Bonds, Base-Ten, Number Lines, Arrays, Fractions, Decimals, GH₵ Money, Clocks, Patterns)

slides.title: 1. Counting 1:1 on a Single Ten Frame (B1)
slides.purpose: Build 7 using one-to-one correspondence on a ten frame.
onScreenText: Tap 7 squares on the ten frame

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0f9ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#075985">1. Counting 1:1 on a Ten Frame</text></svg>

narration.script: Tap seven boxes on the ten frame to show the number seven.

keyIdeas: A ten frame helps you subitise 7 quickly as 5 and 2.

interactive.title: Show 7 on the Ten Frame
interactive.fallbackText: Place 7 counters on a 10-cell frame (5 on top row, 2 on bottom row).

slides.title: 2. Make-10 Addition on a Double Ten Frame (B1/B2)
slides.purpose: Combine 8 blue + 5 amber counters on a double ten frame.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fffbeb"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#92400e">2. Make-10 on a Double Ten Frame</text></svg>

narration.script: Place eight blue counters and five amber counters to see how eight plus five makes thirteen.

keyIdeas: Fill the first ten frame (8 + 2 = 10), then add the remaining 3 to get 13.

interactive.title: Build 8 + 5 on the Double Ten Frame
interactive.instructions: Place 8 blue counters and 5 amber counters.

slides.title: 3. Number Bonds to 10 — Find the Missing Part (B1)
slides.purpose: Part-part-whole number bond: whole 10, part 6, missing part 4.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eef2ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#312e81">3. Number Bonds to 10</text></svg>

narration.script: Find the missing part that pairs with six to make ten.

interactive.title: Complete the Number Bond to 10
interactive.instructions: Set the missing part so both parts sum to 10.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Number bond to 10 with known part 6

slides.title: 4. Number Bonds to 20 — Find the Whole (B2)
slides.purpose: Combine parts 9 and 8 to find whole 17.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdf4"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#14532d">4. Number Bond — Find the Whole</text></svg>

narration.script: Combine parts nine and eight to find the whole.

interactive.title: Find the Whole for 9 and 8
interactive.instructions: Set the whole value that combines 9 and 8.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Number bond finding whole from 9 and 8

slides.title: 5. Base-Ten Place Value — Build 134 (Canonical & Non-Canonical)
slides.purpose: Represent 134 using base-ten blocks; both canonical and regrouped forms accepted.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eff6ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">5. Base-Ten Place Value (134)</text></svg>

narration.script: Build one hundred and thirty-four using hundreds, tens, and ones blocks.

keyIdeas: 10 ones equal 1 ten, so 134 can be regrouped in equivalent ways.

interactive.title: Build 134 with Base-Ten Blocks
interactive.instructions: Add blocks or exchange to represent 134.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Base ten place value mat for 134

slides.title: 6. Base-Ten Regrouping — Exchange to Canonical Form (243)
slides.purpose: Start with 1 hundred, 13 tens, 13 ones (= 243) and regroup into canonical 2-4-3.
onScreenText: Exchange 10 ones -> 1 ten, then 10 tens -> 1 hundred!

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#faf5ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#581c87">6. Regrouping into Canonical Form</text></svg>

narration.script: Use the exchange buttons to regroup the blocks into canonical place-value form for two hundred and forty-three.

keyIdeas: Exchanging preserves total value while putting 0 to 9 blocks in each place.

commonMisconceptions: Changing the total value during regrouping

interactive.title: Regroup 1H + 13T + 13O into Canonical 243
interactive.instructions: Use the Exchange buttons so each column has 0–9 blocks while keeping total 243.

slides.title: 7. Proportional Number Line — Addition Jumps (14 + 23)
slides.purpose: Start at 14 and jump +10, +10, +3 to reach 37.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#ecfeff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#155e75">7. Number Line Addition Jumps</text></svg>

narration.script: Start at fourteen and jump forward by twenty-three to land on thirty-seven.

keyIdeas: Break 23 into +10, +10, +1, +1, +1 on the number line.

interactive.title: Jump from 14 to 14 + 23
interactive.instructions: Use the jump buttons to land on 37.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Number line from 0 to 50 starting at 14

slides.title: 8. Proportional Number Line — Subtraction Backwards (42 − 17)

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fff7ed"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#9a3412">8. Number Line Subtraction</text></svg>

narration.script: Jump backward seventeen units from forty-two.

keyIdeas: Subtraction moves left along a proportional number line.

interactive.title: Jump Back from 42 by 17
interactive.instructions: Use negative jumps to land on 25.

slides.title: 9. Multiplication Arrays — Cocoa Seedlings (4 × 6)
slides.purpose: Build a 4 × 6 (or commutative 6 × 4) array of 24 cocoa seedlings.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdf4"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#14532d">9. Multiplication Arrays (4 × 6)</text></svg>

narration.script: Arrange twenty-four cocoa seedlings in a four-by-six rectangular array.

keyIdeas: Arrays visually prove multiplication is commutative: 4 × 6 = 6 × 4.

interactive.title: Build a 4 × 6 Cocoa Seedling Array
interactive.instructions: Set rows and columns to build a 4 × 6 (or 6 × 4) array.

slides.title: 10. Equal Grouping — Sharing 20 Mangoes Among 4 Baskets

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fefce8"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#854d0e">10. Equal Grouping (20 ÷ 4)</text></svg>

narration.script: Share twenty mangoes equally across four baskets.

keyIdeas: Equal sharing links division directly to multiplication.

interactive.title: Share 20 Mangoes into 4 Equal Baskets
interactive.instructions: Set 4 groups and find how many mangoes belong in each basket.

slides.title: 11. Division with Remainders (17 ÷ 5 = 3 R 2)
slides.purpose: Divide 17 pencils into packs of 5 with remainder < divisor.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fdf2f8"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#9d174d">11. Division with Remainders (17 ÷ 5)</text></svg>

narration.script: Pack seventeen pencils into five equal groups and find the quotient and remainder.

keyIdeas: Dividend = Divisor × Quotient + Remainder, with 0 ≤ Remainder < Divisor.

commonMisconceptions: Leaving a remainder larger than the divisor (e.g. 2 R 7)

interactive.title: Divide 17 by 5 with Remainder
interactive.instructions: Set the quotient per group and the remainder for 17 ÷ 5.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Division with remainder for 17 divided by 5

slides.title: 12. Fraction Bars — Equivalent Fractions (2/3 = 4/6 = 8/12)
slides.purpose: Shade any exact fraction equivalent to 2/3.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0f9ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#075985">12. Equivalent Fraction Bars</text></svg>

narration.script: Shade a fraction bar that is exactly equivalent to two-thirds.

keyIdeas: Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero whole number creates an equivalent fraction.

commonMisconceptions: Adding the same number to numerator and denominator

interactive.title: Shade a Fraction Equivalent to 2/3
interactive.instructions: Shade parts on the bar (e.g. 4/6 or 2/3) to match 2/3.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Fraction bar for equivalent fraction to 2/3

slides.title: 13. Improper Fractions & Mixed Numbers (7/4 = 1 3/4)
slides.purpose: Shade 7 quarters to see 1 whole bar plus 3/4.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eef2ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#312e81">13. Improper & Mixed Fractions</text></svg>

narration.script: Shade seven quarters to see how seven-fourths equals one and three-quarters.

interactive.title: Shade 7/4 (1 3/4) on the Fraction Bar
interactive.instructions: Tap +1 Part seven times to build 7/4.

slides.title: 14. Decimal Place Value Mat — Build 2.35 (B5)
slides.purpose: Represent 2.35 as 2 ones, 3 tenths, 5 hundredths in exact integer hundredths.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdfa"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#134e4a">14. Decimal Place Value (2.35)</text></svg>

narration.script: Build two point three five on the decimal place-value mat.

keyIdeas: Each place to the right is ten times smaller: ones, tenths, hundredths.

interactive.title: Build 2.35 on the Decimal Mat
interactive.instructions: Set Ones, Tenths, and Hundredths to make 2.35.

slides.title: 15. Ghanaian Money — Makola Market Change (GH₵20 − GH₵13.50)
slides.purpose: Make exact change of GH₵6.50 using authentic Bank of Ghana notes and coins.
onScreenText: Item costs GH₵13.50 · Customer pays GH₵20.00

visual.altText: Ghanaian Cedi and Pesewa change tray
visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdf4"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#14532d">15. Ghanaian Currency — Make Change</text></svg>

narration.script: A school book costs thirteen cedis fifty pesewas and you pay with a twenty-cedi note. Count out the exact change of six cedis fifty pesewas.

commonMisconceptions: Forgetting the 50 Gp when subtracting 13.50 from 20

interactive.title: Count Out Change: GH₵20.00 − GH₵13.50
interactive.instructions: Place authentic Ghanaian coins and notes totaling GH₵6.50.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Ghanaian currency tray for GH₵6.50 change
interactive.fallbackText: GH₵5 note + GH₵1 coin + 50 Gp coin = GH₵6.50.

slides.title: 16. Ghanaian Money — Fewest Coins/Notes for GH₵7.70
slides.purpose: Make GH₵7.70 using the minimum 4 pieces (GH₵5 + GH₵2 + 50 Gp + 20 Gp).
onScreenText: Target: GH₵7.70 using the fewest Ghanaian coins/notes possible!

visual.altText: Minimum Ghanaian coins and notes for GH₵7.70
visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fffbeb"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#92400e">16. Fewest Coins & Notes (GH₵7.70)</text></svg>

narration.script: Make seven cedis seventy pesewas using the fewest coins and notes possible.

keyIdeas: Use the largest valid denominations first: GH₵5 + GH₵2 + 50 Gp + 20 Gp = 4 pieces.

commonMisconceptions: Using seven GH₵1 coins instead of GH₵5 + GH₵2

interactive.title: Make GH₵7.70 with the Fewest Pieces
interactive.instructions: Build GH₵7.70 using the minimum number of Ghanaian coins and notes.
interactive.fallbackText: GH₵5 + GH₵2 + 50 Gp + 20 Gp = GH₵7.70 (4 pieces).

slides.title: 17. Analogue Clock — Elapsed Time (8:15 AM + 1 hr 30 min)
slides.purpose: Advance the clock from 8:15 AM to 9:45 AM; notice continuous hour-hand motion.
onScreenText: Assembly starts at 8:15 AM and lasts 1 hour 30 minutes
Watch the hour hand move smoothly between 9 and 10!

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eff6ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">17. Analogue Clock & Elapsed Time</text></svg>

narration.script: School starts at eight fifteen. Advance the clock by one hour and thirty minutes to nine forty-five.

keyIdeas: On a real analogue clock, at 9:45 the hour hand is three-quarters of the way from 9 to 10.

commonMisconceptions: Thinking the hour hand stays fixed on 9 at 9:45

interactive.title: Find the End Time: 8:15 AM + 1 hr 30 min

slides.title: 18. Growing Number Pattern — Add 3 Each Step (B4/B6)

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f5f3ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#4c1d95">18. Growing Number Patterns</text></svg>

narration.script: Find the next two numbers in the growing pattern four, seven, ten, thirteen.

keyIdeas: Identify the constant difference (+3) to predict the next terms.

interactive.title: Continue the Growing Pattern (+3)
interactive.instructions: Tap the next two terms to complete 4, 7, 10, 13, ?, ?.
